item.title: Daily News Briefing - 2026-02-17
item.description:
Daily News Briefing - 2026-02-17
Topics covered: - We begin with developments at ByteDance, which is backpedaling after its Seedance two point zero video generator sparked a major Hollywood backlash - This comes as OpenClaw founder Peter Steinberger joins OpenAI, with CEO Sam Altman announcing the hire and emphasizing that "the future is going to be extremely multi-agent." Altman said Steinberger has "a lot of amazing ideas" about getting AI agents to interact with each other, signaling OpenAI's strategic direction toward systems where multiple AI agents collaborate - Meanwhile, Anthropic and the Pentagon are reportedly in a dispute over acceptable uses of the Claude AI system - A particularly troubling legal development involves longtime NPR host David Greene, who is suing Google over its NotebookLM tool - The AI industry workforce continues to experience significant turbulence - In enterprise AI developments, this week's Equity podcast features Glean CEO Arvind Jain explaining his company's strategic shift from enterprise search tool to what he describes as a middleware layer for enterprise AI
